title: Application Support Engineer (L2/L3)
summary: An application support engineer keeps a company's business applications running in production, fixing issues that the first-line service desk (L1) cannot and finding the root cause of repeat problems. L2 engineers diagnose and work around issues; L3 engineers go deeper into code and data, and the team usually works in shifts with an operations or IT service group.
dailyDuties: Pick up incident tickets and restore service within the agreed time
Monitor overnight batch jobs and rerun failures
Search application logs and run SQL to find the cause of errors
Join major incident calls and update the business
Write root cause reports and track permanent fixes
Automate routine checks with shell scripts
Support releases and check the application after deployment

skills.expectation: Own L2 or L3 support for business applications in production
Query and fix data in Oracle, SQL Server or PostgreSQL
Read logs and check processes on Unix or Linux servers
Write shell scripts to automate checks and fixes
Monitor and rerun batch jobs in Control-M or Autosys
Work incidents, problems and changes through ITIL processes
Join major incident calls and write root cause reports
Use Dynatrace, AppDynamics or similar to find slow or failing services
Send clear updates to users and business teams during outages
Trace recurring faults to their root cause
Read stack traces and Java code for L3 fixes
Check Kafka or MQ queues when messages get stuck
Check pods and deployments for containerised apps
Know banking or payments business flows

certifications.why: Cloud basics for apps moving to AWS
